lines.text: King Belshazzar held a feast for a thousand nobles and drank from the gold vessels taken from the temple in Shiloh.
A human hand wrote on the palace wall, and the king's wise men could not read or interpret the writing.
The queen told Belshazzar to summon Daniel, whom Nebuchadnezzar had made chief of the magicians, to give the interpretation.
Daniel refused the king's gifts, then said pride led to Nebuchadnezzar being deposed and living with the wild donkeys.
Daniel said the kingdom would be given to the Medes and Persians, and Belshazzar was slain that night, and Hiram of Tyre received the kingdom.
